message.content:
Repo: /home/amiad/Desktop/taco-sellm. A team of 3 builds a buyer negotiation agent (Tacto Negotiation Arena; context docs/CONTEXT.md). Remote branches: origin/main, origin/jonathans_branch, origin/omars_branch. Use only read-only git commands (git log, git show, git diff, git branch -a; do NOT checkout, fetch, pull or modify anything). Thoroughness: very thorough.

I need the LEARNING CURVE: which code change produced which measured score change.
1. `git log --format='%h %ad %an %s' --date=format:'%a %H:%M' -- sellm/ arena_kit/` on main: build a chronological table: commit, author, what changed in the agent, and the score measured with it (find the matching [run]/[change] entries in docs/LOG.md and runs/README.md, scoreboard in docs/STATUS.md). Key milestones I know of: kit LLM baseline 61.5; negotiator v1.2 67.5; v1.4 72.4; sellm@7a49c38 72.9; jonathans_branch@67001e7 74.9 (clause offer, P02 0.531->0.725); omars_branch E2g (P18 0.467->0.520), runner one loop per case (P05 0.820). Fill in everything between, including reverted / rejected experiments and their numbers.
2. jonathans_branch vs main: `git log main..origin/jonathans_branch`, `git diff main...origin/jonathans_branch --stat` and the substance of the code diff (sellm/endgame.py clause_offer etc.). Summarize exactly what logic it adds.
3. omars_branch vs main: same. Includes Negotiator.hedged(), idx_recent knob (E2/E2g), runner default one loop per case (--turns), experiments/LEDGER.md, SESSION_HANDOFF.md. Summarize the logic and the measured results; read experiments/LEDGER.md and SESSION_HANDOFF.md on that branch via `git show origin/omars_branch:path`.
4. Per hosted practice case (P01 P02 P03 P04 P05 P07 P08 P10 P11 P18): the best score ever reached, by which agent/commit, and the current main score; the C_open, C_best (from runs/README.md).
5. A list of every experiment that was tried and REJECTED or made things worse, with the number and the reason (e.g. LLM writer 71.6 not repeatable, LLM advisor accept made P01/P18 worse, no qn after sc, contract at horizon P08 0.538, idx argument to hedged supplier P08 0.438, one loop per thread in RFQ 0.665).

Output a structured report (max ~2500 words) with tables. Exact numbers and commit hashes matter.

# runs - every session the team has played

Generated by `scripts/pull-runs`; do not edit by hand. Each session has a `.md` (readable:
all e-mails, the supplier's reasons, the cost breakdown, where the deal lost) and a `.json`
(everything the arena returned, plus the case file and the analysis). Session logs of full
runs are in `runs/logs/`.

## Per case: the yardstick and our best

`C_open` and `C_best` are fixed per case, so any term sheet can be scored offline:
`score = (C_open - C) / (C_open - C_best)` with `arena_kit.total_cost`.

Mean of our best per practice case played: 76.3 (10 cases).

## Every session

Gap = C_deal - C_best. Structure = the most that better non-price terms could have saved at
the deal's price, if the supplier had accepted them. Rest = gap minus structure: what is left
for price and the relationship term. A negative rest means the best non-price terms at this
price would beat C_best, so the supplier would not give all of them at this price.

427	## 2026-10-10 18:59 CEST · Jonathan @ MacBook-Pro-von-Jonathan
428	**[change] --agent sellm now plays sellm/negotiator.py (v1, no LLM): a stateless negotiator with a bounded price path**
429	- Why: the lab-best Calculator knobs score 0.789 on the real sandbox D01 (entry 18:30). The new negotiator scores 0.869, 0.909, 0.909, 0.889 (mean 0.894) on D01, 0 timeouts, final_offer after our 6th message; kit LLM agent there: 0.786. Sessions in runs/sandbox/D01 (label 'ab nego-template'), table experiments/results/2026-10-10-s1-d01-nego.json.
430	- What it does: every move is a pure function of case + threads (our earlier asks are read from the thread, nothing is counted in the object), so a second call for the same state returns the same move, a fresh agent resumes after a crash, and agent.fallback is the agent itself. Path: open a few percent below a target price, concede in equal visible steps, never close the last gap ourselves, accept a final_offer, send its cheaper alternative sheet back to get 'agreed', walk away only when the alternative is the better deal. All in our total cost C.
431	- E-mails come from sellm/writer.py (template: greets the person who signed, one checked argument per e-mail with figure next to its ID). No LLM call yet: LLM wording will be an opt-in experiment (SELLM_WRITER=llm), it is off in the lab and by default.
432	- Files: sellm/negotiator.py, sellm/writer.py, sellm/agent.py (make_agent(package, writer=None, **knobs); the old Calculator knobs stay as CALC_KNOBS), tests/test_negotiator.py (11 tests replaying all 63 real sessions in runs/), experiments/ab_sandbox.py (A/B runner, one loop per thread, labels sessions).
433	- NOT finished: lab stress still shows weaknesses I am fixing now (2 refused accepts in parallel RFQ after a timeout replaced the offer ID; absurd price when it changes the contract length; relationship cost under-estimated when the supplier's opening margin is below the sustainable margin). D02/RFQ not yet played on the real sandbox with it. Do not start a practice run with --agent sellm before the next [change] entry from group A.

# SESSION_HANDOFF - Omar's Claude Code session, Sun 11 Oct 2026 01:45 CEST

Written for the next agent on `omars_branch`. Verified against the repo, `docs/LOG.md`, `GET /v1/me`
and a local test run at 01:41-01:45. Everything not marked otherwise is measured; hypotheses are
labelled. The repo's own memory stays authoritative: `AGENTS.md` (rules, read first),
`docs/CONTEXT.md` (the challenge), `docs/STATUS.md` (now), `docs/LEARNINGS.md`, `docs/LOG.md`.

## 1. Project objective

- **Task:** team sellm's buyer agent for the Tacto Negotiation Arena (EHL Grand Finale 2026). It
  negotiates by e-mail over an HTTP API (`https://arena.tacto.ai/v1`) with Tacto's hosted LLM
  supplier bots for the fictional pump maker Hollerau, and accepts a supplier's standing term sheet
  or walks away. Only term sheets bind; unstated terms close on the supplier's standard terms.
- **Success:** case score = `clip((C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best), 0, 1)`, C = the arena's
  total-cost function (`arena_kit/cost.py`). Broken must-have or a deal worse than the opening = 0;
  no deal = the alternative's score. **Live Final Sun 12:00:** hidden cases in 5 waves of 8 minutes,
  every case weighs the same, points = sum of wave means x 100 (max 500). Practice does not rank.
- **Constraints:** no human in the loop during the final; the agent must never call `/v1/events`,
  `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`, `/results` (or `/v1/...`); one API key, 10 open
  sessions, 10 calls/s; 60 s per message per thread (3 timeouts end a thread), 10 messages per
  thread; code freeze 12:00 (team freeze **11:00**); **the final runs `main`** on Jonathan's MacBook.
  Sunday data release at 08:00 (`uv run arena data`); hidden cases may cite it.

## 2. Current architecture

Execution path (one move):

1. Runner: `sellm/runner.py` (final runner: one loop per thread, waves, closing before the cap,
   resume; `python -m sellm.runner --set final --agent sellm`) or the kit's `arena play|run`
   (`arena_kit/cli.py` -> `arena_kit/play.py`, one thread at a time). Both call `scripts/pull-first`
   before practice runs (not for `--set final`).
2. Agent: `sellm/agent.py:make_agent` -> `sellm/endgame.py:Persistent` (subclass of
   `sellm/negotiator.py:Negotiator`) with `KNOBS = {past_target: True, fast_pay: True}`.
   `SELLM_LLM=shadow|apply` swaps in `sellm/advisor.py:Advised` (LLM writer + verdict); **off by default**.
3. `Negotiator.decide(case, threads, focus)` -> `move()` -> one of ask / hold / take_alternative /
   accept / walk_away -> `message()` (`sellm/writer.py:compose`, template e-mails, no LLM).
   Every move is a pure function of case + threads (resumable after a crash).
4. Ask (`plan()`): structure from `calculator.packages()` (all option combinations priced with C at
   one price; payment days by the dossier's cash persona); target from `aim()`: own-plant should-cost
   (`calculator.supplier_cost`) or a prior share of the opening (`TARGET_SHARE` 0.945/0.88, moved by
   dossier signals), first ask = target x 0.94 (`open_below` 0.06), then steps sized so both prices
   meet after `horizon` 4 of our messages, staying just below its quoted price (`keep_below`).
   Arguments: one new checked fact per e-mail (rival offer > own-plant should-cost > falling index >
   `sellm/claims.py` bank, one per topic, fixed order by case type).
5. Close: accept a `final_offer`/`agreed` standing sheet (never ask after a final offer); walk only
   if the alternative is better. In relationship cases `past_target` keeps asking past our target.
6. Supplier knowledge: `sellm/intel/` (`dossier(sid, parts, case, openings)`: 46 stored dossiers in
   `sellm/dossiers/` + case overlay; never raises) -> cash persona, cost of money, signals;
   `sellm/personas.py` names the personas (description only). Data: `arena_kit/data.py:DataPackage`
   over `data/package` (not in git); `calculator.LOCK` serialises lookups across parallel cases.
7. Lab (no arena): `sellm/lab/` (local API with calibrated engine or LLM suppliers, twins of the played
   suppliers, invented scenarios). Architecture map: https://claude.ai/artifact/XH8RgDAuE42ZZTzNFPD8Ay

## 3. Implementation state

- **Git:** branch `omars_branch` (tracks `origin/omars_branch`) at `a5b363c`, identical to
  `origin/main` at 01:41. Working tree clean before this file. Team rule since 01:20: one branch per
  member for an independent version, shared files (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/`, `runs/`) on `main`, the
  chosen version merged into `main` before 11:00 (`AGENTS.md` section 4); every result names
  `<branch>@<hash>` (section 2).
- **This session's changes (all committed and pushed to `main`):** lock + case facts in
  `sellm/intel` (76be2c8); the dossier now reads all opening e-mails (b4361d2); "no qn after sc"
  tried and reverted (0223875); experiments `experiments/llm_writer.py`, `price_path.py`,
  `price_path_arena.py` with write-ups `LLM-WRITER.md`, `PRICE-PATH.md`; `AGENTS.md` rules (935973a, a5b363c).
- **Agent code since the last measured full run (7a49c38, 72.9):** only a persona log line in
  `sellm/endgame.py`; behaviour unchanged.
- **Unfinished (teammates, on `main`):** Jonathan "P02 arguments" (`experiments/p02_arguments.py`,

- **Known issues:** `uv run ruff check .` reports 1 error in `sellm/lab/p02_c_agents.py` (I001,

# PERSISTENCE - can the agent get more by asking longer and harder? (Sat 22:05-23:00)

Jonathan's question: we accept after 4-6 rounds; a more persistent agent should get more. Tested
one change at a time on the real suppliers, one session each (practice suppliers answer identical
messages with identical numbers). The variants are knobs of a layer in its own file,
`sellm/endgame.py` (all off by default: it then plays exactly like the negotiator; `sellm/negotiator.py`
and `sellm/calculator.py` were not edited). Runner: `experiments/persistence.py`. Rows:
`experiments/results/2026-10-10-persistence.json`. Sessions: `runs/`, labels `PERSIST ...` and `TEST past-target`.
Practice sessions used: 10.

## 1. Who ends a negotiation today

Negotiator v1.4 (@cdd9cf8), the ten practice cases:

| Ended by | Cases | After our messages |
|---|---|---|
| the supplier, with `final_offer` | P02, P03, P04, P05, P07, P08 | 3 to 6 |
| us, target reached (relationship term) | P01 | 4 |
| us, it took our ask or its own second sheet | P10, P11, P18 | 2 to 5 |

So in six of ten cases there is nothing to be persistent about: the supplier says its last word and
a final offer is final (sandbox, Sat 15:50: pushing after it lost one of two deals). The room is in
the four cases we end ourselves.

## 2. Results

Reference = negotiator v1.4 without the layer. `.` = not played.

| Variant | D01 (free) | P01 | P04 | P07 | P08 | P11 | P18 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| reference | 0.921 (0.921-0.947 over four sessions) | 0.915 | 0.860 | 0.747 | 0.549 | 0.778 | 0.467 |
| `past_target` | 0.947 | **0.953** | . | . | . | . | . |
| `past_target` + hold our price (`past_creep=0`) | 0.921 | 0.960 | . | . | . | . | . |
| `past_target` + `creep=0.25` (every step at most a quarter of the gap) | 0.959 | 0.960 | . | . | . | 0.710 | 0.467 |
| the same + `zone=0.009` (ask 0.9 % below its offer once it repeats it) | . | . | 0.860 | . | . | 0.710 | 0.434 |
| first ask closer to its price (`floor_share=0.927`) | D02: 0.441 against 0.567 | . | . | 0.773 | 0.549 (same moves) | . | . |

## 3. Findings

- **P1 (seen twice). Stopping at our target leaves money where the supplier is still moving.** In
  a case with a relationship term the negotiator accepts once the offer is at or below the price
  where our own estimate says total cost is lowest. P01: accepted 135.10; asking once more brought
  133.96 (0.915 -> 0.953). D01: 50.20 -> 50.00 on the same path. The estimate of the supplier's cost
  was too high in three of four checkable cases, so the stop came too early.
- **P2 (seen). A supplier takes an ask about 1 % below its standing offer and counters one further
  away.** P01: 133.69 against its 136.50 (2.1 % below) got a counter of 135.10; 133.70, 133.71 and
  133.96 against 135.10 (1.0 %, 1.0 %, 0.8 %) were taken at once. P18 took 5.50 against 5.60 (1.8 %).
  D01's foundry countered 0.7 % below with a lower offer instead.
- **P3 (seen). That is not a rule to build on: whether it says yes depends on the path.** P11 took
  45.09 against its 45.50 in the reference session and refused the same 45.09 in the zone test,
  where the asks before it were different; Omar measured the same case at 0.710 after a change that
  only replaced one cited fact (22:30). P11's 0.778 is one lucky path.
- **P4 (seen). Slower steps do not make a supplier that has stopped moving move.** P11 stood at
  45.50 for five rounds while our asks crept from 44.34 to 45.01, then said `final_offer`. P04 stood
  at 4.94 whatever we asked (4.62, 4.74, 4.90). Holding our price at D01 (a step of 0.01) got the
  same 50.20 twice: "it gives nothing without a move from us" is true there.
- **P5 (seen). How many rounds a supplier gives depends on how far away our asks are - for one
  supplier.** P07: asks 4.82, 4.98, 5.12 got `final_offer` at the third answer (5.41); asks 5.08,
  5.18, 5.25, 5.31 got a fourth answer (5.37), as the kit agent had (5.36). But the job shop in D02
  follows our level: the closer first ask ended at 15.00 instead of 14.40. One supplier each way,
  so the first ask stays as it is.

## 4. What to adopt

1. **`past_target`, alone.** Replayed over all 239 decision states of the latest full runs (ten
   practice cases, D01, D02) it decides differently in 5 - exactly the ones where the negotiator
   accepted because the target was reached (P01, D01). Everywhere else the moves are identical, so
   nothing else can change. Measured: P01 +0.038, D01 +0.026 on its path. Worst case: the supplier
   says `final_offer` at the offer the negotiator would have accepted anyway. It stops at the
   target of a cost estimate 5 % lower, so it cannot chase a supplier far below its cost.
2. Not `creep`, `zone` or `past_creep`: no gain that survives P11 and P18. The knobs stay in the
   layer, off, with this record.

To switch it on for `--agent sellm`: `sellm/agent.py:make_agent` returns
`sellm.endgame.Persistent(..., past_target=True)` (one line; not done - waiting for Jonathan).

## 5. Open

- The hidden cases: about four of ten practice cases carry a relationship term; the rule acts only
  there, and only when the supplier is still moving at our target.
- P2 suggests that the last ask before a supplier's offer decides the price it takes. Mapping that
  per supplier would need its schedule, which hidden suppliers do not show in advance.

## 6. Four more tests: what a supplier gives for what it wants (Sat 23:10-23:40, 10 practice sessions)

Jonathan's three ideas after reading the suppliers' e-mails: push until a supplier refuses, trade
fast payment for price where the dossier shows a cash problem, trade volume for price where it
wants volume. One session per variant and case; reference = negotiator v1.4 (`past_target` where noted).

| Test | Variant | Result |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | after its `final_offer`, one polite ask 1 % below it (`push_final=0.01`) | **P04: the supplier withdrew, no deal, 0.000 (0.860). P08: withdrew, 0.000 (0.549).** P07: took 5.36 against its 5.41, 0.779 (0.747). Stopped after three. |
| T2 | fastest payment in the first ask for a supplier the dossier calls short of cash (`fast_pay`), with `past_target` | P01: 14 days, 132.96 -> **0.969** (0.953 with `past_target` alone, 0.915 without either) |
| T3 | first ask as two offers of equal cost to us, 30 and 90 days (`pay_probe`) | P18 0.419 (0.467); P05 0.762 (0.66-0.82 over six sessions) |
| T4a | a supplier that wants volume hears the forecast first (`signal_facts`) | P04 0.860 (same); P18 0.430 (0.467) |
| T4b | T4a + a fixed call-off schedule offered in the first e-mail (`soft_give`) | P04 0.860 (same); P18 0.467 (same) |

- **P6 (seen, 2 of 3; with the sandbox 3 of 5). A final offer is final.** "We are withdrawing from
  this negotiation" came after a single ask 0.9-1.0 % below the final offer, with a polite text
  and a verified fact. One lost case costs 0.5-0.9, a won push 0.03: never ask after `final_offer`.
  That also answers where the limit is: at the supplier's own last word, not at its cost.
- **P7 (seen, computed). Fast payment is worth about one percent, where the supplier needs cash.**
  P01 (the dossier holds its letter asking for payment within ten days): every offer was 1.2-2.4
  lower with 14 days than with 30 (139.30 against 141.70, 135.20 against 136.50, 133.90 against
  135.10) and it took 132.96 against 133.96. 16 days cost us 0.36 % of the price; net +0.016.
- **P8 (seen). Two equal-cost offers do not find a better payment term.** P18 answered the 30-day
  offer and ended at 5.50 with 30 days, worse for us than the same 5.50 with 90 days.
- **P9 (seen, computed). Volume is no lever in the term sheet.** A binding volume above the need
  is paid for in full by the cost function (P03: +20 % volume costs 786,803 EUR; it would take a
  price cut of 16.7 %); only two of ten cases let us set it at all. The forecast and a call-off
  schedule in the text did not move the two suppliers the dossier marks as wanting volume. What
  such suppliers did pay for was contract length, which the first ask already carries.

**To adopt from section 6: `fast_pay` together with `past_target`.** Replayed over the 157 decision
states of the latest full runs the pair decides differently only in P01 (first ask with 14 days) and
at D01's accept; everything else is identical. Not adopted: `push_final`, `pay_probe`,
`signal_facts`, `soft_give`.

  lower with 14 days than with 30 (139.30 against 141.70, 135.20 against 136.50, 133.90 against

  offer and ended at 5.50 with 30 days, worse for us than the same 5.50 with 90 days.

# LLM-ADVISOR - the LLM around the code's moves, measured on practice (Sat 23:55 - Sun 00:10)

Jonathan asked for a full practice run with the LLM, tool calling, and a decision with a confidence
on whether to take the supplier's offer, tested on five random cases. 15 practice sessions.
Code: `sellm/advisor.py` (`SELLM_LLM=shadow|apply`, off by default), `sellm/llm.py:chat_tools`, the
e-mail writer of `experiments/llm_writer.py` (Omar). Model `gpt-6-sol`. Rows and every verdict:
`experiments/results/2026-10-11-llm-advisor.json`. Sessions: `runs/practice`, labels `... LLM writer ...`.

## What the model does

1. It writes the e-mail around the move code has fixed (guards: required sentences word for word,
   no new figure, no leak; else the template).
2. It gives a verdict on the supplier's standing offer, A = take it now, B = keep negotiating. It
   can call three functions first: the calculator's cost of any price, the dossier's profile of
   the supplier, the checked facts we have left. The confidence is the probability the model puts on
   its letter, read from the token probabilities - computed, not asked.

## Results

Full run, LLM writes every e-mail, verdict logged only (`shadow`); reference = the same agent with
template e-mails (v1.4 run of 21:58; P01 from the test with both new rules):

| Case | LLM e-mails | template | |
|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | 0.984 | 0.969 | +0.015 |
| P02 | 0.515 | 0.531 | -0.016 |
| P03 | 0.933 | 0.923 | +0.010 |
| P04 | 0.860 | 0.860 | 0 |
| P05 | 0.820 | 0.820 | 0 |
| P07 | 0.766 | 0.747 | +0.019 |
| P08 | 0.493 | 0.549 | -0.056 |
| P10 | 0.562 | 0.647 | -0.085 |
| P11 | 0.778 | 0.778 | 0 |
| P18 | 0.446 | 0.467 | -0.021 |
| **mean** | **71.6** | **72.9** | -1.3 |

- The writer worked as built: 45 of 45 e-mails by the model, none rejected by the guards, 4.3 s
  median (5.5 s max). Verdict: 53, 2.4 s median (4.1 s max), no failure. A move took 6-8 s.
- The wording changes what the supplier answers, in both directions. P10: after the model's e-mail
  the supplier sent its final offer without the second sheet that the template run had sent back
  for 31.90 (0.562 against 0.647).
- With the model writing, a case no longer repeats: P07 scored 0.766 in the full run and 0.740 in
  the next session, P02 0.515 and 0.531.

The verdict:

- Shadow run: 48 of 53 verdicts agree with code (B while code asks, A at a final offer or an
  agreement, each with a probability of 0.86 or more). 5 say "take it now" while code kept asking,
  in P03 (three times; the session ended at the same score) and P01 (twice; after two messages at
  135.60 with p = 0.95, where taking it scores 0.898 and the session went on to 0.984).
- Applied in five cases drawn at random (P01, P02, P05, P07, P18), a sure A (0.85+) before the final
  offer accepts at once: it acted twice. **P01: accepted 135.50 after two messages, 0.864 (0.984 in
  shadow). P18: accepted 5.60 after three messages, 0.401 (0.446).** P02 0.531 and P07 0.740: no
  verdict acted.
- P05 in that batch: 0.250. Not the verdict - all three threads timed out (two bidders withdrew)
  with the kit's one-thread-at-a-time runner while five sessions and the model's 6-8 s per move
  ran. The same agent had 0.820 in the full run. An RFQ with a model in the loop needs the
  runner with one loop per thread, or no model.

## Reading

- An early accept gives up concessions and protects against almost nothing: in the 264 saved
  sessions a supplier withdrew in 10 threads - 6 after timeouts, 3 after we asked again past its
  final offer, and one RFQ bidder (P05, sup:70210) while still open, after three asks about 10 %
  below its price. No supplier of a single-supplier case withdrew before its own final offer. So
  "take it now" has next to nothing to win before a final offer, and after one code accepts anyway.
- The model's reason in P01 was our own cost function: "a further price cut could raise our
  total cost" - the relationship estimate that is 2 % too high there (experiments/PERSISTENCE.md, P1).
  A verdict built on our numbers repeats their error with confidence 0.95.
- Not adopted: the model as writer (-1.3 on the mean, and results stop being repeatable) and the
  verdict as a decision. The layer stays in the repo, off. What it is good for as it is: one
  logged sentence per move on why to take an offer or not, at 2-4 s, without touching the move.
======
# LLM-written e-mails vs the template (lab, Sat 23:28, Omar)

**Result: no gain from LLM wording. Recommendation (not yet decided): keep the template.** Same moves, same term sheets and the same checked
facts; only the e-mail text differed. Against LLM suppliers on the 12 twins the LLM writer scored 62.0
against 65.2 for the template (-3.1 points; better in 2, worse in 5, equal in 5).

## Setup

- Arms: `sellm.agent:make_agent` (what `--agent sellm` plays, template e-mails) and
  `experiments.llm_writer:make_agent` (the same negotiator; `gpt-6-sol` rewrites the e-mail around the
  argument sentence and the offer phrase, which code requires word for word; no new figures, no leak or
  ultimatum, else the template goes out).
- `uv run python -m sellm.lab compare sellm.agent:make_agent experiments.llm_writer:make_agent --supplier llm
  --fixed-twins --invented 0 --test 0 --seeds 1 --think -1 --workers 4 --label llm-writer`
  (report: `runs/lab/20261010-232834-compare-llm-writer/report.md`). The engine supplier ignores wording,
  so only `--supplier llm` can show a difference.
- Calls: 54 writer calls, 115 supplier calls, about 20 for the P18 check below. No failures.

## Per twin

| Twin | Template | LLM writer | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| D01 | 0.913 | 0.913 | 0.000 |
| D02 | 0.631 | 0.658 | +0.027 |
| P01 | 0.827 | 0.798 | -0.029 |
| P02 | 0.281 | 0.170 | -0.110 |
| P03 | 0.942 | 0.943 | +0.001 |
| P04 | 0.860 | 0.860 | 0.000 |
| P05 | 0.304 | 0.304 | 0.000 |
| P07 | 0.818 | 0.805 | -0.013 |
| P08 | 0.484 | 0.484 | 0.000 |
| P10 | 0.660 | 0.633 | -0.027 |
| P11 | 0.676 | 0.693 | +0.017 |
| P18 | 0.421 | 0.181 | -0.240 |
| **Mean** | **65.2** | **62.0** | **-3.1 points** |

## What else was measured

- **The writer is safe and fast enough:** 54 of 54 e-mails passed every guard; 4.3 s median, 6.0 s max per
  call (the 60-second rule is not at risk).
- **The LLM supplier is stable for the same e-mail:** P18 with the template, cached and fresh, gave the same
  deal (0.320). So the differences come from the wording, not from sampling.
- **The size of the effect is not stable:** P18 replayed with `play` (slightly different settings than
  `compare`) gave 0.293 for the LLM writer against 0.320 for the template (-0.027, not -0.240). The sign held.
- **Why it loses** (P18 transcript): the LLM's e-mails are warmer and answer the supplier, but they repeat
  its price ("We appreciate your offer of EUR 5.82 per unit") and concede its points ("We understand your
  concern about material-price risk"). The facts are the same; the position reads softer.

## Limits

- The suppliers are our lab's LLM suppliers (`gpt-6-sol` inside the calibrated engine), not Tacto's bots,
  and the same model wrote our e-mails. One run per twin.
- What would settle it for real: the free sandbox (`case:D01`, `case:D02`, real bots) with
  `experiments/ab_sandbox.py`; the arm `nego-llm` there still writes the template and would need this writer.

## Trap found on the way

The kit and `sellm/llm.py` read the key from `LLM_API_KEY`. A `.env` that only has `OPENAI_API_KEY` makes
every LLM call fail, and the kit's LLM agent then plays the naive move without an error.

# P02-ARGUMENTS - what moves a supplier that has stopped at its limit (Sun 01:20-02:10)
Jonathan's question: other teams close P02 (Nordmark, copper on the 7.5 kW motor) better than we
do, although a lower first ask does not help - so their e-mails must argue better. Collect arguments
from the dossier, the letters and the cost calculation and test three to five of them.
**Result: P02 0.531 -> 0.725 with `--agent sellm` on `jonathans_branch@a49c9b4`.** The lever is not
a better sentence. It is the copper index clause, offered at the price where our total cost is
lowest. Eight practice sessions; runner and variants: `experiments/p02_arguments.py`; rows:
`experiments/results/2026-10-11-p02-arguments.json`; sessions: `runs/practice/P02/`, labels `P02 ARG ...`.
## 1. Where P02 stood
More than ten sessions of four different agents (first ask from 296.77 to 354.43, one to three
facts per e-mail, warm, plain and coercive wording, past renewals, an LLM writing) ended between
371.66 and 371.85 with 90 days, score 0.51-0.53. What the supplier does on a fixed price:
| Our e-mail | Its step (worth to it, EUR) | Its words |
|---|---|---|
| no fact | -0.36 to -0.46 a round, final offer after four messages at 373.65 (0.293) | - |
| order prices 2024 and 2026 (`po`) | -1.11 | "it holds and we took it into account" |
| forecast +11.9 % (`fc`) | -1.91 | "factored this volume increase into our calculation" |
| on-time delivery 90.4 % (`sc`) | -0.21 or 0 | "only allows a small further concession" / "does not change our calculation" |
| complaint (`qn`, `duplicate`) | -0.16 or 0, then `final_offer` | "already taken into account" |
In whatever order: the sum stops at 371.66 with 90 days, and then "below this price we would need
facts, not just a lower number".
## 2. The eight sessions
Each variant is `--agent sellm` plus one change; prices, steps and the close stay the agent's.
| Variant | What was added | Result | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clause5` | first ask with the CU-NOTATION clause, 5 % deadband, at our usual low price (343.47) | it answered 351.45 at once; taken: **0.242** | it pays 5.3 % for the clause; the arena then charged a relationship cost of EUR 119,974 |
| `market` | producer prices of electric motors +1.6 % (`idx:PPI-C2711`), electricity -3.7 % (`idx:PPI-D351`) | 0.394 (372.85) | both `irrelevant`; the forecast in the same e-mail moved it 0.46 instead of 1.91; final offer one message earlier |
| `sister` | order prices and forecast of the 4 kW motor we also buy from it; the contract's 95 % delivery target | 0.319 (373.45) | both `irrelevant`, same damage |
| `volume` | its question "which volume can you commit to?" answered: the contract's 6,110 units are binding, plus a call-off schedule | 0.525 (371.72) | no effect |
| `committee` | the dossier's approval ladder: "please put our proposal before your pricing committee, we are glad to wait" | 0.480 (372.12) | slightly worse |
| `clause5-direct` | first ask 361.35 with the clause (the price of lowest total cost, section 3) | **0.735**: it agreed in its first reply | "an index clause for copper aligns with our mutual interest in risk mitigation" |
| `clause5-raise` | first ask 343.47 with the clause; after its 351.45 we asked 361.35 twice | 0.242: it held 351.45 | "our offer of EUR 351.45 is economically viable and remains our official position" |
| `agent-clause` | the rule as built in (section 4): two sheets, the usual fixed-price ask and the clause at 362.70 | **0.725**: it agreed to the clause sheet at once | the price came from our own estimate, no number of this case in the code |
Not tested, because the data already answers it: faster payment (it chose the 90-day sheet over an
equal-cost 30-day sheet in the session without a dossier, so money is worth less to it than our
8 %), the second-source quote (421.06, dearer than its offer: citing it shows our alternative is
worse), our should-cost (374.95, above its price: it argues for the supplier).
## 3. Why the price has to be chosen
Two deals carry a relationship charge: 822.73 at 371.66 / 90 days fixed, and 119,974.28 at 351.45 /
90 days with the clause. A full cost of **EUR 367.56** at a cost of money of **6.67 %** (the rate
between its own 30- and 90-day sheets) reproduces both to the euro. So:
- 371.66 with 90 days is worth 367.56 to it: the fixed-price wall is its cost floor. No argument,
  tone or first ask goes below it; the brief says so ("never sells below its cost floor").
- A clause is "security, not cash" in the arena's margin. Nordmark gives 5.3 % of the price for it;
  the relationship term then counts the deal as 5.8 % below full cost.
- Total cost with the clause (5 % deadband, 90 days) by price: 351.45 -> 0.243, 356 -> 0.565,
  358 -> 0.670, 360 -> 0.725, **361.35 -> 0.735**, 362.70 -> 0.725, 364 -> 0.695, 366 -> 0.612,
  368 -> 0.486. Below 361 every euro off the price costs more in the relationship term than it saves.
- The other clauses cost us more and gain nothing: best 0.549 with the 3 % deadband, 0.269 without one.
- It never raises a price it has named. The first ask on the clause decides.
Still open: `C_best` lies EUR 12,500 below the best clause deal. On a fixed price that is about
365.95 with 90 days, 1.5 % below its full cost. Nothing tried reaches it.
## 4. The rule in the agent (`clause_offer`, `sellm/endgame.py`)
Conditions, all read from the case and our data:
1. the category goal has a relationship term (`stabilise`, `secure_supply`),
2. `index_clause` is negotiable and the supplier's opening quotes a fixed price,
3. a should-cost of its own plant leaves its opening no more than the sustainable margin. Then a
   fixed price has no room by our own data, and the cost we price the clause with is the highest its
   own quote allows (its opening less the sustainable margin). With a clause its price no longer
   stops at its cost, so an estimate that is too low would squeeze it without anyone noticing.
Then the first e-mail carries two sheets: the usual fixed-price ask, and the clause variant that
costs us least at the price where our total cost, relationship term included, is lowest - provided
that beats the fixed price at which the supplier just covers its cost. One sentence explains the
clause. If the supplier agrees to it, the agent accepts; if it answers on the fixed price, the
negotiation goes on as before; a clause it prices below ours is neither taken while the thread is
open nor followed.
Checks: of the recorded cases only P02 meets the conditions; P01, P03, P04, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18
and D01 are played move for move as without the rule (`tests/test_endgame.py`). P14 (not hosted:
cable with a copper clause, `stabilise`) opens with a clause and is not touched. Practice mean by
replay: 72.9 -> 74.8.

- That the supplier's opening earns at least the sustainable margin (true in D01, P01, P02, P03,
  P10). If its opening were below that, our clause price would be too low and the relationship
  term would cost more than computed.
- That a supplier asked above its own price agrees instead of undercutting (seen twice on P02).
- A supplier that does not want the clause answers on the fixed price; the cost is one sentence.
## 5. For the pitch
"Why did your agent write that?" - it offered a copper clause and then asked for a higher price
than the supplier would have given, because the case's own cost function says a healthy supplier is
worth more than the last euro. Replay: https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/411824454914aa5f; the
counter-example, where the low price was taken: https://arena.tacto.ai/replay/70bff38632e765de.

**Repo state (read-only checks):**
- `main` = `origin/main` = `6374d4e`.

- `origin/jonathans_branch` (tip `cd9dcd1`) is missing only `6374d4e`, a docs-only commit. Tag `best-jonathans_branch-74.9` points to `67001e7`.
- `origin/omars_branch` (tip `dbc9623`) already contains main's HEAD.
- The two branches change different files, so they should merge without conflicts. This is an inference; I did not test a merge.

## 2. jonathans_branch vs main

**Commits** (`main..origin/jonathans_branch`):

**Diff stat:** 7 files, +372 / −13.
- `sellm/endgame.py` +99
- `tests/test_endgame.py` +95
- `sellm/agent.py` (`KNOBS` gets `clause_offer=True`)
- `tests/test_negotiator.py` +2
- `experiments/P02-ARGUMENTS.md`, `p02_arguments.py`, results json

**Logic added to `Persistent`:**
- **`clause_case`** decides whether the rule applies. All of these must hold, otherwise it returns None:
  - the knob is on;
  - `index_clause` is negotiable;
  - the opening's first sheet has a fixed price and no clause;
  - `estimate()` is non-None, which already requires a relationship goal (`RELATIONSHIP_GOALS`) and a priced opening;
  - an own-plant should-cost exists and is at least `value(opening) × (1 − sustainable_margin_pct/100)`. In other words, our own data says a fixed price has no room left.
- **`clause_price`** finds the price where our total cost is lowest, relationship term included. It searches a 601-point grid from 0.85× to 1.0× of the price that pays the supplier exactly its full cost.
- **`clause_sheet`** builds the second offer:
  - our first ask again, with the clause option that costs us least (the widest deadband), at `clause_price`;
  - offered only if it costs us at least 0.2 % less than the fixed price at which the supplier just covers its cost.
- **First e-mail:** carries `[fixed-price ask, clause sheet]` plus one sentence (`CLAUSE_LINE`).
- **Guards:**
  - `structure()`: a clause the supplier prices below `clause_price` is not followed; the agent goes back to the fixed price.
  - `plan()`: our ask on a clause structure is raised to `clause_price`.
  - `plan()`: an open clause offer below `clause_price` sets `enough=False`, so it is not accepted.
- **Tests:** P02 gets the second sheet at the cost-minimal price. P01, P03, P04, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18 and D01 play move for move as before (at least 30 states). The 351.45 clause offer from the clause5-raise session is neither taken nor followed. The agreed clause5-direct sheet is accepted.

**Measured:**
- P02 agent-clause @`5e4e333`: 0.725 (362.70 with the CU-NOTATION clause, 5 % deadband, 90 days, agreed in its first reply).
- Hand-built clause5-direct @`0fab3fd`: 0.735 at 361.35.
- Lab stress @`a49c9b4`: PASS, 816 negotiations, 56.1 (one loop per thread) / 55.6 (sequential).
- Full run @`67001e7`: **74.9**.

**Why it works:** Nordmark's full cost is 367.56, which reproduces both relationship charges exactly. The fixed price of 371.66 at 90 days is its cost floor. A clause buys 5.3 % off the price, but going below about 361 costs more in the relationship term than it saves.

**Negotiator logic:**
- **`contract`** knob (`"longest"` by default). With `"horizon"`, where total cost does not care about contract length, it takes the shortest option that covers the horizon. This is E1, rejected.
- **`idx_recent`** knob (None by default). Set to a percentage, it adds one index argument: a cost-driver index whose yearly change rose but which fell at least that much from its peak of the last 12 months, ranked by weight × change, largest fall only. This is E2.
- **`Negotiator.hedged()`** blocks material-index claims (anything except `LCI-` and `PPI-D35` series) to a supplier with the dossier signal `material_hedged`, and only acts when `idx_recent` is set. This is E2g.
- **`sellm/agent.py` KNOBS are unchanged on the branch**, so E2g is not active in that branch's `--agent sellm`.

**Runner logic:**
- `Limits.serial` puts a `wire` lock around each POST, so one message per session is in flight.
- `Limits.turns` makes one loop per case with no focus: the agent picks the thread (fewest of our messages first), as the kit's `play()` does.
- **Default is now `turns` + `serial`.** `--per-thread` restores the old loops; `--serial` adds one-message-in-flight to them.
